semanticNote: Sighing or rueful interjection — used at the start of a sentence to convey resignation, mild frustration, or wistfulness. Different from 哎 (which calls attention or expresses surprise). Often paired with 沒辦法 or 算了.

examples.chinese: 唉，我又遲到了。
examples.pinyin: Āi, wǒ yòu chídào le.
examples.english: Sigh, I'm late again.

examples.chinese: 唉，這就是人生啊。
examples.pinyin: Āi, zhè jiùshì rénshēng a.
examples.english: Alas, that's just life.

english: to cherish and protect; to take good care of
semanticNote: Combines 愛 (love) and 護 (protect) — to treat something/someone with caring protectiveness, usually applied to public property, animals, the environment, or younger people. Heavier and more formal than 愛 alone; common in signs and public-service language (e.g., 愛護環境). Different from 保護, which is purely 'protect' without the affection.

examples.chinese: 請大家愛護公共財物。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā àihù gōnggòng cáiwù.
examples.english: Please take good care of public property.

examples.chinese: 我們應該愛護動物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi àihù dòngwù.
examples.english: We should cherish and protect animals.

english: to treasure; to use sparingly; to not waste
semanticNote: Means to value something so much that you don't waste or squander it — typical objects are time (時間), life (生命), resources, food, talent. Subtler than 愛護: 愛護 = protect from harm; 愛惜 = use carefully because it's precious. Often appears in moralistic or self-improvement contexts.

examples.chinese: 你要愛惜時間，別浪費。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào àixī shíjiān, bié làngfèi.
examples.english: You should treasure your time and not waste it.

examples.chinese: 他很愛惜這支筆，因為是爸爸送的。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn àixī zhè zhī bǐ, yīnwèi shì bàba sòng de.
examples.english: He treasures this pen because his dad gave it to him.

semanticNote: Literally 'love-heart' — refers to the trait or attitude of compassion and kindness toward others, especially the vulnerable. Common in charity contexts (愛心捐款 charity donation, 愛心便當 free meals for the needy). Not romantic love; closer to English 'a kind heart' or 'compassion.'

examples.chinese: 她對流浪狗很有愛心。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì liúlàng gǒu hěn yǒu àixīn.
examples.english: She has a lot of compassion for stray dogs.

examples.chinese: 謝謝你的愛心捐款。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de àixīn juānkuǎn.
examples.english: Thank you for your charitable donation.

semanticNote: Used both as a verb ('to comfort someone') and as an adjective ('feel consoled / reassuring'). When adjectival it usually follows 感到 or 覺得 — e.g., 感到很安慰 'feel reassured'. Compare 鼓勵 (encourage, push forward) which is forward-looking, vs. 安慰 which soothes existing distress.

examples.chinese: 她哭的時候，我不知道怎麼安慰她。
examples.pinyin: Tā kū de shíhou, wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme ānwèi tā.
examples.english: When she was crying, I didn't know how to comfort her.

examples.chinese: 看到孩子健康成長，父母感到很安慰。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào háizi jiànkāng chéngzhǎng, fùmǔ gǎndào hěn ānwèi.
examples.english: Seeing their children grow up healthy, the parents feel very reassured.

semanticNote: The standard verb for installing — used for both physical equipment (air conditioner, plumbing) and software/apps. In Taiwan tech contexts you'll hear it constantly: 安裝軟體, 安裝程式, 安裝 App. Don't confuse with 裝 alone (more colloquial, can also mean 'to pretend').

examples.chinese: 我幫你安裝這個軟體。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bāng nǐ ānzhuāng zhè ge ruǎntǐ.
examples.english: I'll install this software for you.

examples.chinese: 工人正在安裝冷氣。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài ānzhuāng lěngqì.
examples.english: The workers are installing the air conditioner.

semanticNote: Bound morpheme — rarely stands alone in modern speech. Almost always appears in compounds: 河岸 (riverbank), 海岸 (seacoast), 岸邊 (by the shore), 上岸 (to come ashore / get off a boat / quit a bad habit). Politically loaded too: 兩岸 = 'the two shores,' shorthand for Mainland-Taiwan relations.

examples.chinese: 我們在河岸邊散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài hé'àn biān sànbù.
examples.english: We took a walk by the riverbank.

examples.chinese: 船終於靠岸了。
examples.pinyin: Chuán zhōngyú kào àn le.
examples.english: The boat finally reached the shore.

semanticNote: Single-character adjective with two related senses: (1) physically dark / dim (opposite of 亮); (2) hidden, covert (暗號 secret signal, 暗戀 secret crush). The 'secret' sense is very productive in compounds. As a stand-alone descriptor of light it can take 很/太/有點: 房間有點暗.

examples.chinese: 房間太暗了，開個燈吧。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān tài àn le, kāi ge dēng ba.
examples.english: The room's too dark — turn on a light.

examples.chinese: 他暗暗喜歡她很多年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā àn'àn xǐhuān tā hěn duō nián le.
examples.english: He's secretly liked her for many years.

english: to stay up late; to pull an all-nighter
semanticNote: Separable V-O construction (熬 endure + 夜 night) — literally 'to endure the night.' Can split: 熬了一夜, 熬一個晚上的夜. Carries the connotation of suffering through, not just being awake — different from 晚睡 (sleep late). Hugely common in student/work life talk.

examples.chinese: 我昨天熬夜趕報告，今天好累。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān áoyè gǎn bàogào, jīntiān hǎo lèi.
examples.english: I pulled an all-nighter on a report yesterday — I'm exhausted today.

examples.chinese: 他熬了一整夜的夜，眼睛都紅了。
examples.pinyin: Tā áole yì zhěng yè de yè, yǎnjīng dōu hóng le.
examples.english: He stayed up the whole night — his eyes are all red.

english: to grasp, to seize (an opportunity); confidence, certainty (n.)
semanticNote: Two main uses: (1) verb 'to seize/grasp' — 把握機會 (seize the opportunity), 把握時間 (make the most of time); (2) noun 'confidence/certainty' — 有把握 (be confident), 沒把握 (not sure). Note: the noun sense is about your inner certainty about an outcome, not general self-confidence (that's 自信).

examples.chinese: 你一定要把握這次機會。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yídìng yào bǎwò zhè cì jīhuì.
examples.english: You absolutely have to seize this opportunity.

examples.chinese: 我對考試沒什麼把握。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì kǎoshì méi shénme bǎwò.
examples.english: I don't feel very confident about the exam.

english: to place, to arrange, to set out; to sway
semanticNote: Versatile verb. Core sense: place items in an arranged way (擺桌子 set the table, 擺攤 set up a stall). Secondary sense: sway/wave (鐘擺 pendulum, 擺手 wave one's hand). Also figurative — 擺架子 'put on airs'. Stronger spatial-arrangement nuance than 放, which just means 'put down.'

examples.chinese: 媽媽把碗筷擺在桌上。
examples.pinyin: Māma bǎ wǎnkuài bǎi zài zhuō shàng.
examples.english: Mom set the bowls and chopsticks on the table.

examples.chinese: 他在夜市擺了一個小攤。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yèshì bǎile yí ge xiǎo tān.
examples.english: He set up a small stall at the night market.

english: to handle, to process, to deal with (paperwork/procedures)
semanticNote: Formal/official register — used specifically for processing paperwork, formalities, or institutional procedures: 辦理手續 (process paperwork), 辦理登記 (register), 辦理簽證 (process a visa). You'll see it on bank/government counter signs everywhere in Taiwan. More formal than plain 辦.

examples.chinese: 請到三號櫃台辦理登記。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dào sān hào guìtái bànlǐ dēngjì.
examples.english: Please go to counter three to register.

examples.chinese: 我明天要去銀行辦理開戶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào qù yínháng bànlǐ kāihù.
examples.english: I'm going to the bank tomorrow to open an account.

semanticNote: Refers to the period right before dark — roughly 5–7pm depending on season. More poetic / slightly more formal than 晚上 (evening) and narrower than it. Compare 黃昏 (more literary, 'twilight'). Can function as a time adverb without 在: 傍晚我們去散步.

examples.chinese: 傍晚的時候，海邊特別漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Bàngwǎn de shíhou, hǎibiān tèbié piàoliang.
examples.english: The seaside is especially beautiful at dusk.

examples.chinese: 我們傍晚六點在公園見。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bàngwǎn liù diǎn zài gōngyuán jiàn.
examples.english: Let's meet at the park at six in the early evening.

semanticNote: Primarily a noun in everyday speech ('package, parcel') — what arrives from the post office or courier. As a verb means to wrap something up (often medically: 包裹傷口 dress a wound). Don't confuse with 包包 (bag, handbag) or 行李 (luggage).

examples.chinese: 我收到一個從美國寄來的包裹。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōudào yí ge cóng Měiguó jì lái de bāoguǒ.
examples.english: I got a package sent from America.

examples.chinese: 護士小心地包裹他的傷口。
examples.pinyin: Hùshì xiǎoxīn de bāoguǒ tā de shāngkǒu.
examples.english: The nurse carefully wrapped his wound.

semanticNote: Subtle but real difference from 包括: 包含 stresses what's contained inside a thing (intrinsic content — meanings, ingredients, components), while 包括 enumerates members of a list. 'This dish contains peanuts' = 包含; 'The team includes John, Mary, Sue' = 包括. They overlap, but 包含 leans abstract/contents-of, 包括 leans listing.

examples.chinese: 這道菜包含花生，過敏的人別吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài bāohán huāshēng, guòmǐn de rén bié chī.
examples.english: This dish contains peanuts — don't eat it if you're allergic.

examples.chinese: 他的話裡包含著很深的意思。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà lǐ bāohán zhe hěn shēn de yìsi.
examples.english: His words contain a very deep meaning.

semanticNote: Used to enumerate members of a set — 'X includes A, B, and C.' Often paired with 在內 ('inclusive') for emphasis: 包括我在內 'including me.' See contrast with 包含 (intrinsic contents) at card 2415. Very high-frequency in writing and formal speech.

examples.chinese: 費用包括住宿和早餐。
examples.pinyin: Fèiyòng bāokuò zhùsù hé zǎocān.
examples.english: The fee includes lodging and breakfast.

examples.chinese: 包括我在內，一共有五個人去。
examples.pinyin: Bāokuò wǒ zàinèi, yígòng yǒu wǔ ge rén qù.
examples.english: Including me, five people are going in total.

semanticNote: Heteronym alert. Two readings: (1) báo — physical thinness (thin paper, thin slice, thin clothing), the colloquial reading and the one locked here; (2) bó — abstract/literary 'slim, meager, weak,' as in 薄弱 (weak), 薄情 (heartless), 微薄 (meager). Rule of thumb: in casual spoken Chinese describing tangible thickness, use báo. Opposite is 厚 hòu.

examples.chinese: 今天穿這件衣服太薄了，會冷。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān chuān zhè jiàn yīfu tài báo le, huì lěng.
examples.english: Wearing this shirt today is too thin — you'll be cold.

examples.chinese: 請把肉切得薄一點。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ ròu qiē de báo yìdiǎn.
examples.english: Please slice the meat a bit thinner.

semanticNote: Two registers: (1) literal 'treasured object / valuable thing' — 這是我的寶貝相機; (2) term of endearment for kids, partners, pets — exactly like English 'baby' or 'sweetie.' In Taiwan parents say 寶貝 to small children constantly. Can also be used slightly mockingly for someone overprotective of a possession.

examples.chinese: 寶貝，快來吃飯。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobèi, kuài lái chīfàn.
examples.english: Sweetie, come eat.

examples.chinese: 這台相機是我的寶貝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái xiàngjī shì wǒ de bǎobèi.
examples.english: This camera is my treasure.

semanticNote: Used for abstract precious things — time, life, experience, opinions, advice (寶貴的時間/意見/經驗). For physical valuables, 珍貴 or 貴重 are more natural. Slightly formal/written register; in casual speech 很重要 or 很珍貴 is more common.

examples.chinese: 謝謝你寶貴的意見。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ bǎoguì de yìjiàn.
examples.english: Thank you for your valuable opinion.

examples.chinese: 時間是最寶貴的。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān shì zuì bǎoguì de.
examples.english: Time is the most precious thing.

english: to maintain, to keep (a state, habit, condition)
semanticNote: Used to keep an existing state going — 保持安靜 (stay quiet), 保持聯絡 (stay in touch), 保持距離 (keep your distance), 保持健康 (stay healthy). Different from 保留 (retain, hold on to) and 維持 (sustain, often barely). 保持 implies actively keeping something at the same level.

examples.chinese: 請大家保持安靜。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā bǎochí ānjìng.
examples.english: Please everyone keep quiet.

examples.chinese: 我們要保持聯絡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎochí liánluò.
examples.english: Let's stay in touch.

english: to save, to store, to preserve (data, food, items)
semanticNote: General-purpose 'preserve, save, keep' — for food, data, documents, historical relics. Pairs with 食物 (food), 文件 (files), 紀錄 (records). Note: in Taiwan tech contexts 儲存 is the menu term for computer 'save', but 保存 remains the general everyday word. More formal/written-register than 留 (keep) or 放 (put/place).

examples.chinese: 這份文件請好好保存。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn qǐng hǎohǎo bǎocún.
examples.english: Please keep this document safely.

examples.chinese: 冰箱可以保存食物。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng kěyǐ bǎocún shíwù.
examples.english: Refrigerators can preserve food.

english: to retain; to reserve; to hold back (an opinion)
semanticNote: Three flavors: (1) keep / not get rid of — 保留傳統 (preserve traditions); (2) reserve / set aside — 保留座位 (reserve a seat); (3) hold back / not fully express — 保留意見 (reserve judgment). Sense 3 is idiomatic and common in formal discussion. Don't confuse with 保持 (maintain a state) or 儲存/保存 (store).

examples.chinese: 我幫你保留一個位子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bāng nǐ bǎoliú yí ge wèizi.
examples.english: I'll save you a seat.

examples.chinese: 對這件事，我保留我的意見。
examples.pinyin: Duì zhè jiàn shì, wǒ bǎoliú wǒ de yìjiàn.
examples.english: On this matter, I'll reserve my opinion.

semanticNote: Mainly the noun 'insurance' — 買保險 (buy insurance), 健康保險 / 健保 (health insurance), 車險 (auto insurance). As an adjective means 'safe / a sure thing': 比較保險 'safer (course of action)'. Note 保險箱 = 'safe' (the box). Common collocation: 保險起見 'just to be safe.'

examples.chinese: 你買健康保險了嗎？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ mǎi jiànkāng bǎoxiǎn le ma?
examples.english: Have you bought health insurance?

examples.chinese: 保險起見，我們提早一個小時出發。
examples.pinyin: Bǎoxiǎn qǐjiàn, wǒmen tízǎo yí ge xiǎoshí chūfā.
examples.english: Just to be safe, let's leave an hour early.

english: to check in; to report for duty / registration
semanticNote: Separable V-O verb (報 'report' + 到 'arrival') — 'report your arrival.' Used for officially registering your presence: school enrollment, conference check-in, hotel check-in for an event, military report-for-duty. Splits with aspect markers and quantifiers: 報了到, 報過到. Different from 簽到 (sign in / mark attendance, no registration step).

examples.chinese: 新生明天到學校報到。
examples.pinyin: Xīnshēng míngtiān dào xuéxiào bàodào.
examples.english: New students check in at the school tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 我已經報了到，現在可以進去了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng bàole dào, xiànzài kěyǐ jìnqù le.
examples.english: I've already checked in — I can go in now.

english: to report (news); news report, news coverage
semanticNote: Taiwan media style: trad is 報導 with 導 (dǎo, to lead/guide) — pronounced bàodǎo. Mainland writes 報道 with 道 (dào, way) — pronounced bàodào. Different characters, different readings, same meaning: 'to report on (news), news coverage'. Both verb and noun. Pairs with 新聞 (news), 媒體 (media).

examples.chinese: 記者正在報導這場比賽。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě zhèngzài bàodǎo zhè chǎng bǐsài.
examples.english: The reporter is covering this match.

examples.chinese: 今天的新聞報導很詳細。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de xīnwén bàodǎo hěn xiángxì.
examples.english: Today's news coverage is very detailed.

english: report, presentation (n.); to report, to present (v.)
semanticNote: Both noun and verb. Noun = a formal report or presentation, very common in school/work (期末報告 final paper/presentation, 工作報告 work report). Verb = to formally report or brief someone. Different from 報導 (news coverage). In Taiwan classrooms 做報告 = 'do a presentation,' a constant student phrase.

examples.chinese: 下週我要交期末報告。
examples.pinyin: Xiàzhōu wǒ yào jiāo qímò bàogào.
examples.english: Next week I have to turn in my final report.

examples.chinese: 請你向老闆報告一下進度。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ xiàng lǎobǎn bàogào yíxià jìndù.
examples.english: Please report the progress to the boss.

semanticNote: Refers to the organization/office that produces a newspaper, not the paper itself (that's 報紙). 社 here means 'society / agency' (same 社 as 社會). Compare 出版社 publisher, 旅行社 travel agency. With media moving online, the term still applies to the publishing organization.

examples.chinese: 他在報社當記者。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bàoshè dāng jìzhě.
examples.english: He works as a reporter at a newspaper.

examples.chinese: 這家報社有一百多年的歷史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā bàoshè yǒu yìbǎi duō nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This newspaper agency has over a hundred years of history.

semanticNote: To verbally complain or grumble about something — generally negative tone. Different from 投訴 (file a formal complaint) and 埋怨 (resentful complaining, often about someone close). Object can be a thing complained about (抱怨工作) or a person complained at (向他抱怨). Often + 一直/老 to mark habitual complaining.

examples.chinese: 他老是抱怨工作太忙。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǎoshì bàoyuàn gōngzuò tài máng.
examples.english: He's always complaining that work is too busy.

examples.chinese: 別抱怨了，做點實際的事吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié bàoyuàn le, zuò diǎn shíjì de shì ba.
examples.english: Stop complaining and do something practical.

english: back (of body); to recite from memory; to turn one's back on
semanticNote: Heteronym alert. Locked reading bèi covers: (1) noun 'back of body / back side' (背痛 backache, 背後 behind); (2) verb 'recite from memory' (背書 / 背單字 memorize words); (3) verb 'turn one's back on / behind one's back' (背叛 betray). The other reading bēi means 'to carry on one's back' (背小孩 carry a child on the back, 背包 backpack). Context disambiguates.

examples.chinese: 明天考試，我得背一百個單字。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān kǎoshì, wǒ děi bèi yìbǎi ge dānzì.
examples.english: Tomorrow's the test — I have to memorize a hundred words.

examples.chinese: 我的背好痛，可能是坐太久了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de bèi hǎo tòng, kěnéng shì zuò tài jiǔ le.
examples.english: My back hurts a lot — probably from sitting too long.

semanticNote: Direct opposite of 樂觀 (optimistic) — they're a fixed pair and almost always taught together. Describes someone's outlook or attitude toward a situation. Common pattern: 對 X 感到/覺得悲觀 'feel pessimistic about X.' Slightly formal-flavored but used in everyday speech as well.

examples.chinese: 他對未來太悲觀了。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì wèilái tài bēiguān le.
examples.english: He's too pessimistic about the future.

examples.chinese: 別這麼悲觀，事情還沒那麼糟。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhème bēiguān, shìqing hái méi nàme zāo.
examples.english: Don't be so pessimistic — things aren't that bad yet.

semanticNote: Covers both literal backdrop (stage/photo setting) and figurative context or backing. 家庭背景 (family background), 政治背景 (political background/backing). In Taiwan, 有背景 (has backing/connections) implies powerful patrons — a social reality in business and politics.

examples.chinese: 在理解這首詩之前，先了解作者的時代背景很重要。
examples.pinyin: Zài lǐjiě zhè shǒu shī zhīqián, xiān liǎojiě zuòzhě de shídài bèijǐng hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Before understanding this poem, it's important to first understand the historical context of the author.

examples.chinese: 他有深厚的藝術背景，從小學習鋼琴和繪畫。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu shēnhòu de yìshù bèijǐng, cóngxiǎo xuéxí gāngqín hé huìhuà.
examples.english: He has a solid artistic background, having studied piano and painting since childhood.

semanticNote: The standard word for a bed quilt or duvet. 蓋被子 (cover yourself with a quilt), 曬被子 (air out the quilt in the sun). Airing quilts on sunny days is a common household practice in Taiwan — a sign of 勤勞 (diligence).

examples.chinese: 天氣變涼了，記得多蓋一條被子。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì biàn liáng le, jìde duō gài yī tiáo bèizi.
examples.english: The weather has turned cool — remember to add an extra quilt.

examples.chinese: 媽媽趁著大晴天把被子拿出去曬。
examples.pinyin: Māma chènzhe dà qíngtiān bǎ bèizi ná chūqù shài.
examples.english: Mom took advantage of the sunny day to air out the quilts.

semanticNote: The standard term for undergraduate education and the bachelor's degree. 本科生 (undergraduate student), 本科學位 (bachelor's degree). Contrasts with 研究所/碩士 (master's) and 博士 (PhD). Taiwan's university entrance via 學測 or 指考 leads to 本科 programs.

examples.chinese: 她本科念的是經濟學，研究所改讀法律。
examples.pinyin: Tā běnkē niàn de shì jīngjìxué, yánjiūsuǒ gǎi dú fǎlǜ.
examples.english: She studied economics for her undergraduate degree, then switched to law for graduate school.

examples.chinese: 申請這份工作最低學歷要求是本科畢業。
examples.pinyin: Shēnqǐng zhè fèn gōngzuò zuìdī xuélì yāoqiú shì běnkē bìyè.
examples.english: The minimum educational requirement to apply for this job is a bachelor's degree.

semanticNote: A hands-on, practical skill or innate capability — something earned through practice or inherent talent. 有本領 (capable; skilled), 真本領 (real ability; the real deal). More concrete and earned than 能力 (general ability). Has a slightly old-fashioned, martial-arts-story flavor in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 他有真本領，不用靠關係就能把事情做好。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu zhēn běnlǐng, bùyòng kào guānxi jiù néng bǎ shìqíng zuòhǎo.
examples.english: He has real ability — he can get things done without relying on connections.

examples.chinese: 要在這行出頭，光有學歷不夠，還要有真本領。
examples.pinyin: Yào zài zhè háng chūtóu, guāng yǒu xuélì bùgòu, hái yào yǒu zhēn běnlǐng.
examples.english: To succeed in this field, credentials alone aren't enough — you need real capability.

semanticNote: The fundamental, unchanging nature of something — contrasted with surface appearance (表面). 本質上 (essentially; at its core), 認清本質 (see the true nature of something). Common in philosophical, political, and analytical writing. 萬變不離其宗 — the essence remains even when the form changes.

examples.chinese: 雖然形式不同，但這兩個問題的本質是一樣的。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xíngshì bùtóng, dàn zhè liǎng gè wèntí de běnzhì shì yīyàng de.
examples.english: Although the forms differ, the essence of these two problems is the same.

examples.chinese: 我們要看清事情的本質，而不是只看表面現象。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào kànqīng shìqíng de běnzhì, ér bùshì zhǐ kàn biǎomiàn xiànxiàng.
examples.english: We need to see the true nature of things, not just look at surface phenomena.

semanticNote: Used in math (比例關係 — proportional relationship), maps (比例尺 — map scale), and statistics (比例很高 — the proportion is high). 按比例 (in proportion; proportionally). Common in academic, scientific, and policy writing.

examples.chinese: 這所學校男女生的比例大約是六比四。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào nánnǚshēng de bǐlì dàyuē shì liù bǐ sì.
examples.english: The ratio of male to female students in this school is approximately six to four.

examples.chinese: 城市人口占全國的比例逐年上升。
examples.pinyin: Chéngshì rénkǒu zhàn quánguó de bǐlì zhúnián shàngshēng.
examples.english: The proportion of the urban population as a share of the national total has been rising year by year.

english: each other; one another; both sides
semanticNote: A formal reciprocal pronoun — slightly more literary than 互相 (mutually). 彼此了解 (understand each other), 彼此彼此 (same to you; we're in the same boat — a playful set phrase used as a humble response to a compliment). The reduplicated form 彼此彼此 is very common in Taiwan conversation.

examples.chinese: 雖然認識時間不長，但彼此已經建立了深厚的信任。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán rènshi shíjiān bù cháng, dàn bǐcǐ yǐjīng jiànlì le shēnhòu de xìnrèn.
examples.english: Although they haven't known each other long, they've already built a deep mutual trust.

examples.chinese: 「謝謝你的幫忙。」「彼此彼此！」
examples.pinyin: "Xièxiè nǐ de bāngmáng." "Bǐcǐ bǐcǐ!"
examples.english: "Thank you for your help." "Likewise! We're in the same boat!"

english: inevitable; certain; necessary; bound to happen
semanticNote: Stronger and more philosophical than 一定 — implies logical or historical necessity. 必然結果 (inevitable result), 歷史的必然 (historical inevitability). Common in academic argumentation. Contrasts with 偶然 (accidental; coincidental).

examples.chinese: 付出努力不一定保證成功，但不努力必然失敗。
examples.pinyin: Fùchū nǔlì bù yīdìng bǎozhèng chénggōng, dàn bù nǔlì bìrán shībài.
examples.english: Putting in effort doesn't guarantee success, but not trying inevitably leads to failure.

examples.chinese: 經濟發展帶來環境問題，這似乎是必然的代價。
examples.pinyin: Jīngjì fāzhǎn dài lái huánjìng wèntí, zhè sìhū shì bìrán de dàijià.
examples.english: Economic development bringing environmental problems seems to be an inevitable price.

semanticNote: Practical necessity — something that must exist or be done for a goal to be achieved. 有必要 (there is a need to; it's necessary to), 沒有必要 (there's no need to; unnecessary). More practical than 必然 (logically inevitable). 有必要嗎？ is a common rhetorical challenge.

examples.chinese: 在做決定之前，有必要聽取各方意見。
examples.pinyin: Zài zuò juédìng zhīqián, yǒu bìyào tīngqǔ gè fāng yìjiàn.
examples.english: Before making a decision, it's necessary to hear opinions from all sides.

examples.chinese: 這麼小的事有必要大驚小怪嗎？
examples.pinyin: Zhème xiǎo de shì yǒu bìyào dà jīng xiǎo guài ma?
examples.english: Is it really necessary to make such a big fuss over something so small?

english: after all; when all is said and done; in the end
semanticNote: A concessive adverb that acknowledges an unchangeable reality — 畢竟她還是個孩子 (after all, she's still a child). Used to soften a statement or concede a point while reframing it. More formal and written than 到底 in this sense. Very common in reasoning and persuasion.

examples.chinese: 他雖然犯了錯，但畢竟是第一次，可以給他機會改正。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán fàn le cuò, dàn bìjìng shì dì yī cì, kěyǐ gěi tā jīhuì gǎizhèng.
examples.english: Although he made a mistake, it's his first offense after all — he can be given a chance to correct it.

examples.chinese: 畢竟我們認識了這麼多年，彼此都很了解。
examples.pinyin: Bìjìng wǒmen rènshi le zhème duō nián, bǐcǐ dōu hěn liǎojiě.
examples.english: After all, we've known each other for so many years — we understand each other well.

english: to avoid; to avert; to prevent
semanticNote: To deliberately avoid or steer clear of something undesirable. 避免衝突 (avoid conflict), 避免誤會 (prevent misunderstandings), 避免不了 (unavoidable; can't be helped). More purposeful than 躲避 (evade/hide from). Common in formal advice, policy, and interpersonal guidance.

examples.chinese: 出門前先查看天氣預報，可以避免被突如其來的大雨淋濕。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián xiān cháchá tiānqì yùbào, kěyǐ bìmiǎn bèi tūrú qílái de dàyǔ lín shī.
examples.english: Checking the weather forecast before going out can help you avoid getting soaked by sudden heavy rain.

examples.chinese: 要避免誤會，最好把話說清楚。
examples.pinyin: Yào bìmiǎn wùhuì, zuìhǎo bǎ huà shuō qīngchǔ.
examples.english: To avoid misunderstandings, it's best to speak clearly.

semanticNote: Both the action (to edit, compile) and the person (an editor). 文字編輯 (copy editor), 影片編輯 (video editor). In Taiwan's digital media landscape, 編輯 covers print editors and digital content editors alike. 總編輯 (editor-in-chief) is the top role at a publication.

examples.chinese: 這本雜誌的主編輯在業界有很高的聲望。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn zázhì de zhǔ biānjí zài yèjiè yǒu hěn gāo de shēngwàng.
examples.english: The chief editor of this magazine has a very high reputation in the industry.

examples.chinese: 她花了一週時間編輯這支影片。
examples.pinyin: Tā huā le yī zhōu shíjiān biānjí zhè zhī yǐngpiàn.
examples.english: She spent a week editing this video.

semanticNote: The traditional string firecrackers used at Lunar New Year, weddings, store openings, and temple festivals. 放鞭炮 (set off firecrackers). In Taiwan, 鞭炮 are still widely used at temples despite noise concerns. The sound is considered auspicious — believed to drive away evil spirits (驅邪).

examples.chinese: 除夕夜午夜，街上到處響起鞭炮聲，熱鬧非凡。
examples.pinyin: Chúxī yè wǔyè, jiē shàng dàochù xiǎngqǐ biānpào shēng, rènào fēifán.
examples.english: At midnight on Lunar New Year's Eve, the sound of firecrackers erupted everywhere in the streets — festive and lively.

examples.chinese: 廟會期間信徒放鞭炮，祈求神明庇佑。
examples.pinyin: Miàohuì qījiān xìntú fàng biānpào, qíqiú shénmíng bìyòu.
examples.english: During the temple fair, worshippers set off firecrackers to pray for the gods' blessings.

semanticNote: Heteronym: biàn = convenient, ordinary, then/so (就便 — since you're at it); pián = cheap (便宜 pián yi). As adverb, 便 is a literary equivalent of 就 — 她一回家便開始做飯 (the moment she got home, she started cooking). Taiwan formal writing uses 便 frequently in this literary adverb sense.

examples.chinese: 他下班後便直接去接孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàbān hòu biàn zhíjiē qù jiē háizi.
examples.english: After getting off work, he went straight to pick up the children.

examples.chinese: 這個社區交通方便，生活機能完善。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shèqū jiāotōng fāngbiàn, shēnghuó jīnéng wánshàn.
examples.english: This neighborhood has convenient transportation and comprehensive amenities.

english: to debate; to argue; a debate
semanticNote: Structured argumentation or a formal debate. 辯論賽 (debate competition — very popular in Taiwan schools and universities), 辯論雙方 (both sides of the debate). More formal than 爭論 (argue, dispute). Taiwan's university debate culture (辯論社) is lively and competitive.

examples.chinese: 她參加了校際辯論賽，表現出色，獲得最佳辯士獎。
examples.pinyin: Tā cānjiā le xiàojì biànlùn sài, biǎoxiàn chūsè, huòdé zuìjiā biànshì jiǎng.
examples.english: She participated in the interscholastic debate competition, performed outstandingly, and won the Best Debater award.

examples.chinese: 兩位專家就氣候變遷問題展開了激烈辯論。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng wèi zhuānjiā jiù qìhòu biànqiān wèntí zhǎnkāi le jīliè biànlùn.
examples.english: Two experts engaged in a heated debate on the issue of climate change.

semanticNote: Refers to punctuation marks collectively. 標點符號 (punctuation marks — the full term), 加標點 (add punctuation). Classical Chinese had no punctuation; modern punctuation was standardized in the 20th century. Taiwan uses full-width punctuation marks (。，、！？) and different conventions from mainland China (e.g., 「」for quotes instead of "" ).

examples.chinese: 寫作時要注意正確使用標點符號。
examples.pinyin: Xiězuò shí yào zhùyì zhèngquè shǐyòng biāodiǎn fúhào.
examples.english: When writing, pay attention to using punctuation marks correctly.

examples.chinese: 他的文章標點有誤，讀起來令人困惑。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wénzhāng biāodiǎn yǒu wù, dú qǐlái lìng rén kùnhuò.
examples.english: His article had punctuation errors that made it confusing to read.

english: sign; symbol; mark; logo; to symbolize
semanticNote: Both concrete (a logo, a road sign, a landmark) and abstract (an event that marks/symbolizes something). 品牌標誌 (brand logo), 標誌性建築 (iconic/landmark building), 標誌著新時代的開始 (marks the beginning of a new era). Common in branding, architecture, and formal writing.

examples.chinese: 台北101是台灣最具標誌性的建築之一。
examples.pinyin: Táiběi yī líng yī shì Táiwān zuì jù biāozhì xìng de jiànzhú zhī yī.
examples.english: Taipei 101 is one of Taiwan's most iconic landmarks.

examples.chinese: 這場演講標誌著她政治生涯的正式開始。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yǎnjiǎng biāozhì zhe tā zhèngzhì shēngyá de zhèngshì kāishǐ.
examples.english: This speech marked the official beginning of her political career.

english: to express; to convey; to communicate (feelings/ideas)
semanticNote: The act of communicating inner feelings, thoughts, or ideas outwardly. 表達感謝 (express gratitude), 表達能力 (communication/expression skills), 語言表達 (verbal expression). One of the most commonly assessed skills in Taiwan's school curriculum — 口語表達 (spoken expression) and 書面表達 (written expression).

examples.chinese: 她不善於用言語表達感情，但行動上非常體貼。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù shànyú yòng yányǔ biǎodá gǎnqíng, dàn xíngdòng shàng fēicháng tǐtiē.
examples.english: She's not good at expressing her feelings verbally, but she's very thoughtful in her actions.

examples.chinese: 這幅畫清楚地表達了作者對自由的渴望。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà qīngchǔ de biǎodá le zuòzhě duì zìyóu de kěwàng.
examples.english: This painting clearly expresses the artist's longing for freedom.

semanticNote: Literal (the surface of something) and figurative (the superficial/outward appearance). 表面上 (on the surface; outwardly), 表面現象 (surface phenomena; superficial appearance). 表面工夫 (superficial effort; going through the motions) is a common Taiwanese idiom for doing things just for show.

examples.chinese: 表面上他很樂觀，但內心其實很孤獨。
examples.pinyin: Biǎomiàn shàng tā hěn lèguān, dàn nèixīn qíshí hěn gūdú.
examples.english: On the surface he seems optimistic, but deep down he's actually very lonely.

examples.chinese: 不要只看表面，要深入了解問題的根本原因。
examples.pinyin: Bùyào zhǐ kàn biǎomiàn, yào shēnrù liǎojiě wèntí de gēnběn yuányīn.
examples.english: Don't just look at the surface — go deeper to understand the root cause of the problem.

english: to make clear; to state clearly; to indicate; to demonstrate
semanticNote: To make one's position or a fact explicitly clear — often in formal or official contexts. 表明立場 (state one's position/stance), 表明態度 (make one's attitude clear). More declarative and final than 表示 (indicate/express). Government statements and diplomatic language use 表明 frequently.

examples.chinese: 政府發表聲明，表明不接受任何外部干涉。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fābiǎo shēngmíng, biǎomíng bù jiēshòu rènhé wàibù gānshè.
examples.english: The government issued a statement, making clear that it does not accept any external interference.

examples.chinese: 她的行動已清楚表明她對這個計畫的支持。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xíngdòng yǐ qīngchǔ biǎomíng tā duì zhège jìhuà de zhīchí.
examples.english: Her actions have clearly demonstrated her support for this plan.

semanticNote: The expression on one's face. 面無表情 (expressionless), 表情豐富 (very expressive). In Taiwan digital culture, 表情符號 and 表情包 (emoji / sticker packs) use the word in its extended digital sense — LINE貼圖 (LINE stickers) are ubiquitous. Reading 表情 is a key social skill: 看她的表情就知道 (you can tell just by her expression).

examples.chinese: 他聽到這個消息時，臉上的表情複雜難以言喻。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīng dào zhège xiāoxi shí, liǎn shàng de biǎoqíng fùzá nán yǐ yányù.
examples.english: When he heard the news, the expression on his face was complex and hard to put into words.

examples.chinese: 她面無表情地聽著，讓人猜不透她在想什麼。
examples.pinyin: Tā miàn wú biǎoqíng de tīng zhe, ràng rén cāi bù tòu tā zài xiǎng shénme.
examples.english: She listened expressionlessly, making it impossible to tell what she was thinking.

english: to show; to display; performance; behavior; manifestation
semanticNote: Both the action (to show/perform) and the result (one's performance/behavior). 工作表現 (job performance), 表現優異 (outstanding performance), 表現自我 (express oneself). The nuance between 表現 (show/perform) and 表達 (communicate/express) is subtle: 表現 is behavioral/observable, 表達 is communicative.

examples.chinese: 他這次考試表現得非常好，讓老師感到驚喜。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhè cì kǎoshì biǎoxiàn de fēicháng hǎo, ràng lǎoshī gǎndào jīngxǐ.
examples.english: He performed very well on this exam, which pleasantly surprised the teacher.

examples.chinese: 藝術家透過作品表現內心深處的情感。
examples.pinyin: Yìshùjiā tòuguò zuòpǐn biǎoxiàn nèixīn shēnchù de qínggǎn.
examples.english: Artists express the deep emotions of their inner world through their works.

semanticNote: Taiwan uses 冰淇淋 (bīngqílín) in everyday speech; the simplified form 冰激凌 (bīngjīlíng) is the mainland standard. Both refer to ice cream. Taiwan's shaved ice desserts (剉冰, 雪花冰) are distinct from 冰淇淋, though both appear at 冰店 (ice dessert shops).

examples.chinese: 炎熱的夏天，吃一球冰淇淋真的很消暑。
examples.pinyin: Yánrè de xiàtiān, chī yī qiú bīngjīlíng zhēn de hěn xiāoshǔ.
examples.english: On a sweltering summer day, eating a scoop of ice cream is truly refreshing.

examples.chinese: 她最喜歡抹茶口味的冰淇淋。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuān mǒchá kǒuwèi de bīngjīlíng.
examples.english: Her favorite flavor of ice cream is matcha.

semanticNote: Covers both biological viruses (流感病毒 — influenza virus, 新冠病毒 — COVID-19 virus) and computer viruses (電腦病毒). 病毒式傳播 (viral spreading — used for content going viral). Taiwan's experience with SARS (2003) and COVID-19 made 病毒 a high-frequency word in public discourse.

examples.chinese: 這種病毒傳播速度極快，需要盡快採取防疫措施。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú chuánbō sùdù jí kuài, xūyào jǐnkuài cǎiqǔ fángyì cuòshī.
examples.english: This virus spreads extremely quickly, and preventive measures need to be taken as soon as possible.

examples.chinese: 他的電腦中了病毒，所有文件都遭到損壞。
examples.pinyin: Tā de diànnǎo zhòng le bìngdú, suǒyǒu wénjiàn dōu zāodào sǔnhuài.
examples.english: His computer got a virus and all the files were damaged.

semanticNote: The material glass, and by extension glassware or glass objects. 玻璃杯 (glass cup), 玻璃窗 (glass window), 打碎玻璃 (break glass). In Taiwan internet slang, 玻璃心 (glass heart) means overly thin-skinned or easily hurt — a very common expression among younger generations.

components.meaning: (phonetic component in 玻璃; also: coloured glaze)

examples.chinese: 不小心把玻璃杯打翻，碎片散落了一地。
examples.pinyin: Bù xiǎoxīn bǎ bōli bēi dǎfān, suìpiàn sànluò le yī dì.
examples.english: Accidentally knocked over a glass, sending shards scattering across the floor.

examples.chinese: 這棟大樓外牆全是玻璃帷幕，看起來非常現代。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu wàiqiáng quán shì bōli wéimù, kànqǐlái fēicháng xiàndài.
examples.english: The exterior wall of this building is entirely glass curtain wall, giving it a very modern appearance.

english: to broadcast; to play (audio/video); to transmit
semanticNote: To air, broadcast, or play media content — radio, TV, streaming. 播放音樂 (play music), 播放清單 (playlist), 直播 (live broadcast/stream — now dominant in Taiwan streaming culture). Used for both traditional broadcasting and digital streaming contexts.

examples.chinese: 電台每天早上七點開始播放新聞。
examples.pinyin: Diàntái měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn kāishǐ bōfàng xīnwén.
examples.english: The radio station starts broadcasting the news at seven o'clock every morning.

examples.chinese: 她把自己最喜歡的歌曲加入播放清單，反覆聆聽。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zìjǐ zuì xǐhuān de gēqǔ jiārù bōfàng qīngdān, fǎnfù língtīng.
examples.english: She added her favorite songs to the playlist and listened to them on repeat.

semanticNote: The everyday colloquial word for neck (compare 頸部 — the formal/anatomical term). 脖子酸痛 (stiff/sore neck — very common complaint from office workers and phone users), 圍巾圍在脖子上 (wrap a scarf around the neck). 脖子 is used in casual speech; medical contexts prefer 頸部 or 頸椎.

examples.chinese: 長時間看電腦，她的脖子又酸又痛。
examples.pinyin: Cháng shíjiān kàn diànnǎo, tā de bózi yòu suān yòu tòng.
examples.english: After staring at the computer for a long time, her neck was stiff and sore.

examples.chinese: 天氣冷了，記得圍條圍巾保護脖子。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì lěng le, jìde wéi tiáo wéijīn bǎohù bózi.
examples.english: Now that it's cold, remember to wear a scarf to protect your neck.

semanticNote: The standard term for a museum. Taiwan has world-class museums including the National Palace Museum (國立故宮博物院) — home to one of the world's greatest collections of Chinese art and artifacts. 博物院 (palace museum/court museum) vs 博物館 (general museum) — the distinction is formal but 博物館 covers both in casual usage.

examples.chinese: 故宮博物院是台灣最受歡迎的觀光景點之一。
examples.pinyin: Gùgōng Bówùyuàn shì Táiwān zuì shòu huānyíng de guānguāng jǐngdiǎn zhī yī.
examples.english: The National Palace Museum is one of Taiwan's most popular tourist attractions.

examples.chinese: 她每次到新城市旅遊都一定會參觀當地的博物館。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi cì dào xīn chéngshì lǚyóu dōu yīdìng huì cānguān dāngdì de bówùguǎn.
examples.english: Every time she visits a new city, she always makes sure to visit the local museum.

english: to replenish; to supplement; to add; supplementary
semanticNote: To fill in what's lacking — adding to a stock, supplementing information, or topping up. 補充說明 (supplement with an explanation; add a note), 補充水分 (replenish fluids), 補充維生素 (take vitamin supplements). Very common in academic, health, and business contexts.

examples.chinese: 運動後要及時補充水分，避免脫水。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng hòu yào jíshí bǔchōng shuǐfèn, bìmiǎn tuōshuǐ.
examples.english: After exercise, replenish fluids promptly to avoid dehydration.

examples.chinese: 老師講完之後，有同學舉手補充了一些重要資訊。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiǎng wán zhīhòu, yǒu tóngxué jǔshǒu bǔchōng le yīxiē zhòngyào zīxùn.
examples.english: After the teacher finished, a student raised their hand to add some important information.

semanticNote: A mild-to-moderate sense of unease or anxiety — between 擔心 (worried) and 恐懼 (fearful). 感到不安 (feel uneasy), 社會不安 (social unrest), 惴惴不安 (full of anxiety — a set phrase). Note the apostrophe: bù'ān, not bùān — because 安 starts with a vowel.

examples.chinese: 考試前夕，她感到惴惴不安，難以入睡。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì qiányè, tā gǎndào zhuìzhuì bù'ān, nányǐ rùshuì.
examples.english: On the eve of the exam, she felt full of anxiety and couldn't fall asleep.

examples.chinese: 這樣的社會治安狀況讓居民感到不安。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng de shèhuì zhì'ān zhuàngkuàng ràng jūmín gǎndào bù'ān.
examples.english: This kind of public security situation makes residents feel uneasy.

semanticNote: Emphasizes continuity without interruption. Common in formal writing and news. 不斷地 + verb is a frequent pattern. Stronger and more literary than 一直.

examples.chinese: 她不斷地練習，終於在比賽中拿到了冠軍。
examples.pinyin: Tā búduàn de liànxí, zhōngyú zài bǐsài zhōng ná dào le guànjūn.
examples.english: She kept practicing without stopping and finally won the championship.

examples.chinese: 科技不斷進步，改變了我們的生活方式。
examples.pinyin: Kējì búduàn jìnbù, gǎibiàn le wǒmen de shēnghuó fāngshì.
examples.english: Technology keeps advancing, changing the way we live.

semanticNote: Challenges an assumption or expectation; softer than 不一定. Often follows a stated opinion to politely push back. More colloquial than formal.

examples.chinese: 貴的東西不見得就是好的。
examples.pinyin: Guì de dōngxi bújiàndé jiùshì hǎo de.
examples.english: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

examples.chinese: 他雖然很努力，但不見得能通過考試。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán hěn nǔlì, dàn bújiàndé néng tōngguò kǎoshì.
examples.english: Even though he works hard, he's not necessarily going to pass the exam.

semanticNote: Describes visible impatience or irritation at delay or repetition. Often shows in behavior: 不耐煩地揮手 (wave dismissively). Slightly negative connotation; contrast with 有耐心.

examples.chinese: 等了半小時，他開始顯得不耐煩了。
examples.pinyin: Děng le bàn xiǎoshí, tā kāishǐ xiǎndé búnàifán le.
examples.english: After waiting half an hour, he started to look impatient.

examples.chinese: 媽媽不耐煩地說：「我已經說過三遍了！」
examples.pinyin: Māmā búnàifán de shuō: 'Wǒ yǐjīng shuō guò sān biàn le!'
examples.english: Mom said impatiently, 'I've already said it three times!'

semanticNote: Introduces a consequence if the preceding condition is not met: 'otherwise.' Also used as 'if not so; if that's not the case.' Very common in speech; equivalent to 要不然 in informal registers.

examples.chinese: 快點出發吧，不然會趕不上火車的。
examples.pinyin: Kuàidiǎn chūfā ba, bùrán huì gǎn bú shàng huǒchē de.
examples.english: Let's get going—otherwise we'll miss the train.

examples.chinese: 你得多穿幾件，不然容易著涼。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ děi duō chuān jǐ jiàn, bùrán róngyì zháoliáng.
examples.english: You should put on more layers, otherwise you'll easily catch a cold.

semanticNote: Indicates A is inferior to B, or proposes an alternative: 不如 + suggestion (= 'better to...'). Both meanings are common and important for the exam. The suggestion use is especially frequent in conversation.

examples.chinese: 他的中文不如他姊姊說得流利。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén bùrú tā jiějie shuō de liúlì.
examples.english: His Chinese isn't as fluent as his older sister's.

examples.chinese: 與其等計程車，不如走路去，反而更快。
examples.pinyin: Yǔqí děng jìchéngchē, bùrú zǒulù qù, fǎn'ér gèng kuài.
examples.english: Rather than waiting for a taxi, it's better to walk—it's actually faster.

semanticNote: A reassuring phrase: 'it doesn't matter; it's not serious; never mind.' Used to play down a problem or console someone. Very common in casual speech. Contrast with 要緊 (serious; important).

examples.chinese: 「對不起，我遲到了。」「不要緊，我也才剛到。」
examples.pinyin: 'Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le.' 'Bú yàojǐn, wǒ yě cái gāng dào.'
examples.english: 'Sorry I'm late.' 'No worries, I just got here too.'

examples.chinese: 不要緊，這件事沒你想的那麼嚴重。
examples.pinyin: Bú yàojǐn, zhè jiàn shì méi nǐ xiǎng de nàme yánzhòng.
examples.english: It's okay—this matter isn't as serious as you think.

semanticNote: Formal word for 'insufficient; lacking.' Used for quantities, funds, evidence, sleep, etc. 不足以 + verb = 'not enough to...' Common in written reports and formal speech in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 這份報告的資料不足，需要補充更多數據。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào de zīliào bùzú, xūyào bǔchōng gèng duō shùjù.
examples.english: The data in this report is insufficient; more figures need to be added.

examples.chinese: 她因睡眠不足，整天都無法集中注意力。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn shuìmián bùzú, zhěng tiān dōu wúfǎ jízhōng zhùyìlì.
examples.english: Because of insufficient sleep, she couldn't concentrate all day.

semanticNote: As a noun: fabric, cloth. As a verb: to spread, to announce, to deploy (troops, a net, a plan). The verb sense is formal and often appears in compounds: 佈置 (to arrange; decorate), 公佈 (to announce publicly), 散佈 (to spread; distribute). Taiwan commonly uses 佈 for the verb sense.

examples.chinese: 裁縫師傅用這塊布做了一件漂亮的旗袍。
examples.pinyin: Cáifeng shīfu yòng zhè kuài bù zuò le yī jiàn piàoliang de qípáo.
examples.english: The tailor used this piece of cloth to make a beautiful qipao.

examples.chinese: 政府公佈了最新的防疫措施。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ gōngbù le zuìxīn de fángyì cuòshī.
examples.english: The government announced the latest epidemic prevention measures.

semanticNote: Refers to individual steps in a process or procedure; more formal than 步 alone. Often appears in instructions, tutorials, and reports. 按步驟 (step by step) is a very common pattern.

examples.chinese: 請按照以下步驟安裝軟體。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào yǐxià bùzhòu ānzhuāng ruǎntǐ.
examples.english: Please follow the steps below to install the software.

examples.chinese: 做蛋糕的步驟看似簡單，但每一步都要精確。
examples.pinyin: Zuò dàngāo de bùzhòu kànsì jiǎndān, dàn měi yī bù dōu yào jīngquè.
examples.english: The steps for making a cake seem simple, but each one needs to be precise.

semanticNote: General term for a department or division within an organization (government, company, institution). In Taiwan government contexts, 部門 often refers to ministry-level bodies. Contrast with 科 (section) and 處 (office/division).

examples.chinese: 這個問題涉及多個部門，需要跨部門協調。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí shèjí duō gè bùmén, xūyào kuà bùmén xiétiáo.
examples.english: This issue involves multiple departments and requires cross-departmental coordination.

examples.chinese: 她在財政部門工作了十五年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cáizhèng bùmén gōngzuò le shíwǔ nián.
examples.english: She has worked in the finance department for fifteen years.

semanticNote: Refers to property and assets broadly — real estate, money, valuables. A legal and formal term. Taiwan uses 財產 in legal documents and everyday speech. Compare 財富 (wealth, riches — more abstract) and 資產 (assets — accounting/business register).

examples.chinese: 遺囑中明確說明了財產的分配方式。
examples.pinyin: Yízhǔ zhōng míngquè shuōmíng le cáichǎn de fēnpèi fāngshì.
examples.english: The will clearly stated how the property would be distributed.

examples.chinese: 離婚時，夫妻雙方必須協商共同財產的歸屬。
examples.pinyin: Lí hūn shí, fūqī shuāngfāng bìxū xiéshāng gòngtóng cáichǎn de guīshǔ.
examples.english: When divorcing, both parties must negotiate the ownership of jointly held property.

semanticNote: To interview (journalistic); to gather news. As a noun: an interview or news-gathering mission. Primarily a journalism/media term. 接受採訪 (to give an interview), 採訪記者 (reporter on assignment). Taiwan spelling: 採訪.

components.meaning: to pick; to gather; to select
to visit; to interview; to inquire

examples.chinese: 記者去採訪了這次地震的倖存者。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě qù cǎifǎng le zhè cì dìzhèn de xìngcúnzhě.
examples.english: The reporter went to interview survivors of the earthquake.

examples.chinese: 這位導演很少接受媒體採訪。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi dǎoyǎn hěn shǎo jiēshòu méitǐ cǎifǎng.
examples.english: This director rarely gives media interviews.

semanticNote: Formal verb meaning to adopt, take, or employ (measures, policies, attitudes, positions). Always followed by an abstract noun: 採取措施 (take measures), 採取行動 (take action). Not used for physical objects. Taiwan spelling: 採取.

components.meaning: to pick; to take; to adopt
to take; to fetch; to obtain

examples.chinese: 政府決定採取嚴厲措施，以遏制通貨膨脹。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng cǎiqǔ yánlì cuòshī, yǐ èzhì tōnghuò péngzhàng.
examples.english: The government decided to take strict measures to curb inflation.

examples.chinese: 面對批評，他採取了開放的態度，願意傾聽。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì pīpíng, tā cǎiqǔ le kāifàng de tàidù, yuànyì qīngtīng.
examples.english: Facing criticism, he adopted an open attitude and was willing to listen.

semanticNote: Rainbow. Beyond the literal sense, 彩虹 is widely used in Taiwan as a symbol of LGBTQ+ pride (彩虹旗 = rainbow flag), hope after hardship, and children's imagery. 雨後彩虹 (rainbow after the rain) is a common metaphor for resilience.

examples.chinese: 雨剛停，天空出現了一道美麗的彩虹。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ gāng tíng, tiānkōng chūxiàn le yī dào měilì de cǎihóng.
examples.english: The rain had just stopped and a beautiful rainbow appeared in the sky.

examples.chinese: 台北每年都會舉辦彩虹驕傲遊行，吸引大批民眾參與。
examples.pinyin: Táiběi měi nián dōu huì jǔbàn cǎihóng jiāo'ào yóuxíng, xīyǐn dà pī mínzhòng cānyù.
examples.english: Taipei holds a Rainbow Pride parade every year, drawing large crowds of participants.

semanticNote: To step on; to tread; to stamp. Carries a sense of pressure or deliberate contact with the foot. Common in both literal (踩到釘子 — step on a nail) and figurative uses (踩線 — cross a line; push a boundary).

examples.chinese: 他不小心踩到了小狗的腳，狗叫了一聲。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn cǎi dào le xiǎogǒu de jiǎo, gǒu jiào le yī shēng.
examples.english: He accidentally stepped on the puppy's paw and it yelped.

examples.chinese: 請不要踩草坪，謝謝配合。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào cǎi cǎopíng, xièxiè pèihé.
examples.english: Please do not walk on the lawn. Thank you for your cooperation.

semanticNote: To consult or refer to (sources, data, opinions) for guidance. As a noun: reference material. 參考書 (reference book), 參考資料 (reference material), 供參考 (for your reference) are all common in Taiwan academic and business contexts.

components.meaning: to participate; to refer to; consult
to examine; to study; to consider

examples.chinese: 寫論文時，你應該多參考學術期刊上的文章。
examples.pinyin: Xiě lùnwén shí, nǐ yīnggāi duō cānkǎo xuéshù qīkān shàng de wénzhāng.
examples.english: When writing a thesis, you should refer more to articles in academic journals.

examples.chinese: 這份資料僅供參考，不代表官方立場。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn zīliào jǐn gōng cānkǎo, bù dàibiǎo guānfāng lìchǎng.
examples.english: This material is for reference only and does not represent an official position.

semanticNote: Formal: to participate in or be involved in something, especially decision-making or civic activity. More formal and weighty than 參加. 公民參與 (civic participation), 參與決策 (participate in decision-making) are common in Taiwan's public discourse.

components.meaning: and; with; to give; to participate

examples.chinese: 鼓勵市民積極參與地方政府的政策討論。
examples.pinyin: Gǔlì shìmín jījí cānyù dìfāng zhèngfǔ de zhèngcè tǎolùn.
examples.english: Citizens are encouraged to actively participate in local government policy discussions.

examples.chinese: 這個計畫需要各部門共同參與，才能順利完成。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà xūyào gè bùmén gòngtóng cānyù, cái néng shùnlì wánchéng.
examples.english: This project requires joint participation from all departments to proceed smoothly.

semanticNote: Ashamed of one's own shortcomings or failures — specifically the shame felt when one falls short of one's own standards or those of others. More literary than 不好意思. Often appears in formal self-deprecating expressions. Taiwan traditional: 慚愧.

examples.chinese: 他沒能完成任務，感到非常慚愧。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi néng wánchéng rènwù, gǎndào fēicháng cánkuì.
examples.english: He felt deeply ashamed for not being able to complete the task.

examples.chinese: 慚愧，這次考試我讓老師失望了。
examples.pinyin: Cánkuì, zhè cì kǎoshì wǒ ràng lǎoshī shīwàng le.
examples.english: I'm ashamed—I let my teacher down on this exam.

semanticNote: Playground or school sports field; also a military drill ground. In Taiwan, 操場 is most commonly the open area at a school where students run, exercise, and have PE class. Equivalent to 運動場 in more formal or venue contexts.

components.meaning: to drill; to exercise; to conduct

examples.chinese: 每天早上學生們會在操場上做早操。
examples.pinyin: Měi tiān zǎoshang xuéshengmen huì zài cāochǎng shàng zuò zǎocāo.
examples.english: Every morning students do morning exercises on the school field.

examples.chinese: 體育課在操場上課，遇到下雨就改到室內體育館。
examples.pinyin: Tǐyù kè zài cāochǎng shàngkè, yù dào xià yǔ jiù gǎi dào shìnèi tǐyùguǎn.
examples.english: PE class is held on the field; when it rains, it moves to the indoor gym.

semanticNote: To worry about; to take care of — with a sense of ongoing concern or effort. Often implies the subject is investing mental energy into managing someone else's affairs or a difficult situation. Common in speech; mildly affectionate in parental contexts.

components.meaning: to manage; to handle; to worry

examples.chinese: 媽媽總是為孩子的功課操心。
examples.pinyin: Māmā zǒngshì wèi háizi de gōngkè cāo xīn.
examples.english: Mom is always worrying about her children's schoolwork.

examples.chinese: 你別為我操心了，我已經長大了，可以照顧自己。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié wèi wǒ cāo xīn le, wǒ yǐjīng zhǎng dà le, kěyǐ zhàogù zìjǐ.
examples.english: Don't worry about me anymore—I've grown up and can take care of myself.

semanticNote: A book, volume, or booklet. Used as a measure word for books and volumes: 一冊 (one volume). Less common as a standalone noun; more often in compounds: 手冊 (handbook; manual), 畫冊 (picture book; album), 紀念冊 (commemorative album). Taiwan traditional: 冊.

examples.chinese: 公司發給每位新員工一本員工手冊。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī fā gěi měi wèi xīn yuángōng yī běn yuángōng shǒucè.
examples.english: The company gives each new employee an employee handbook.

examples.chinese: 這套叢書共三冊，我已經讀完了第一冊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào cóngshū gòng sān cè, wǒ yǐjīng dú wán le dì yī cè.
examples.english: This series has three volumes; I've already finished the first one.

semanticNote: Test or exam, usually shorter and less formal than 考試. As a verb: to test, to assess. Used for classroom quizzes, diagnostic tests, and skill assessments. 小測驗 (quiz; short test) is common in Taiwan schools. Taiwan traditional: 測驗.

components.meaning: to measure; to survey; to test
to examine; to verify; to test

examples.chinese: 老師說下週會有一次單字測驗，要大家好好複習。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shuō xià zhōu huì yǒu yī cì dāncì cèyàn, yào dàjiā hǎohǎo fùxí.
examples.english: The teacher said there will be a vocabulary test next week and everyone should review carefully.

examples.chinese: 這個線上測驗可以幫助你了解自己的學習程度。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiànshàng cèyàn kěyǐ bāngzhù nǐ liǎojiě zìjǐ de xuéxí chéngdù.
examples.english: This online test can help you understand your own level of learning.

semanticNote: Indicates that something happened at some point in the past — 'once; at one time; used to.' It is always used with completed or past actions, not ongoing states. Often evokes a sense of distance from the past, sometimes wistful. Taiwan traditional: 曾經.

components.meaning: to pass through; to experience; scripture

examples.chinese: 他曾經住在台南，對那裡的小吃非常熟悉。
examples.pinyin: Tā céngjīng zhù zài Táinán, duì nàlǐ de xiǎochī fēicháng shúxī.
examples.english: He once lived in Tainan and is very familiar with the local snacks there.

examples.chinese: 這棟建築曾經是日治時代的官邸。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng jiànzhú céngjīng shì Rìzhì shídài de guāndǐ.
examples.english: This building was once an official residence during the Japanese colonial era.

semanticNote: Fork (the utensil). Everyday noun. Taiwan uses Western cutlery commonly in restaurants. The character 叉 also means a cross/X shape, and appears in 打叉 (put an X; mark as wrong). Distinguish from 筷子 (chopsticks) and 湯匙 / 勺子 (spoon).

examples.chinese: 她習慣用叉子和刀子吃牛排。
examples.pinyin: Tā xíguàn yòng chāzi hé dāozi chī niúpái.
examples.english: She's used to eating steak with a fork and knife.

examples.chinese: 桌上擺著一套刀叉，但我還是選擇用筷子。
examples.pinyin: Zhuō shàng bǎi zhe yī tào dāochā, dàn wǒ háishì xuǎnzé yòng kuàizi.
examples.english: There was a set of cutlery on the table, but I still chose to use chopsticks.

semanticNote: Gap or disparity between two things — often income, performance, ability, or opportunity. A neutral to slightly negative term. Very common in policy and social discourse in Taiwan: 貧富差距 (wealth gap), 城鄉差距 (urban-rural divide), 縮小差距 (narrow the gap).

examples.chinese: 台灣的貧富差距在過去幾十年間持續擴大。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de pínfù chājù zài guòqù jǐ shí nián jiān chíxù kuòdà.
examples.english: The wealth gap in Taiwan has continued to widen over the past few decades.

examples.chinese: 兩隊之間的實力差距比預期的還要大。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng duì zhī jiān de shílì chājù bǐ yùqī de hái yào dà.
examples.english: The gap in strength between the two teams was bigger than expected.

semanticNote: To insert, stick in, or plug in. Covers a wide range: 插花 (flower arranging), 插座 (power outlet), 插嘴 (to interrupt; butt in), 插隊 (cut in line). The sense of thrusting something into a space — literal or social — runs through all uses.

components.meaning: to insert; to stick in; to plug in

examples.chinese: 請把充電線插進手機，等它充飽電再用。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chōngdiànxiàn chā jìn shǒujī, děng tā chōng bǎo diàn zài yòng.
examples.english: Please plug the charger into the phone and wait for it to fully charge before using it.

examples.chinese: 大人在說話，小孩子不要插嘴。
examples.pinyin: Dàrén zài shuōhuà, xiǎoháizi búyào chā zuǐ.
examples.english: Adults are talking—children shouldn't interrupt.

semanticNote: To dismantle, tear apart, or demolish. Used for packages (拆包裹), buildings (拆房子), and gifts (拆禮物). 拆穿 means to expose or debunk. Contrast with 破壞 (destroy maliciously) — 拆 is more neutral and purposeful.

components.meaning: to dismantle; to tear; to open (a package)

examples.chinese: 他迫不及待地拆開生日禮物。
examples.pinyin: Tā pòbùjídài de chāi kāi shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: He couldn't wait to unwrap his birthday present.

examples.chinese: 舊社區的房屋將被拆除，改建為公園。
examples.pinyin: Jiù shèqū de fángwū jiāng bèi chāichú, gǎijiàn wéi gōngyuán.
examples.english: The houses in the old neighborhood will be demolished and replaced with a park.

semanticNote: Product or goods — things produced for sale or use. Very common in business contexts. Distinguish from 作品 (artistic/creative work) and 成果 (result/achievement). 農產品 (agricultural products), 工業產品 (industrial goods) are common compound forms.

examples.chinese: 這家公司研發的新產品在市場上受到熱烈歡迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yánfā de xīn chǎnpǐn zài shìchǎng shàng shòudào rèliè huānyíng.
examples.english: The new product developed by this company has been warmly received in the market.

examples.chinese: 台灣的農產品以高品質著稱，受到許多國家喜愛。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de nóngchǎnpǐn yǐ gāo pǐnzhì zhùchēng, shòudào xǔduō guójiā xǐ'ài.
examples.english: Taiwan's agricultural products are renowned for their high quality and are popular in many countries.

semanticNote: To produce, generate, or give rise to — used for effects, results, feelings, or new entities emerging from a process. Unlike 生產 (to manufacture), 產生 is for abstract outcomes: 產生影響 (have an effect), 產生誤解 (cause a misunderstanding). Very common in academic and formal writing.

components.meaning: to arise; to be born; to generate

examples.chinese: 長期使用手機會對眼睛產生不良影響。
examples.pinyin: Chángqī shǐyòng shǒujī huì duì yǎnjing chǎnshēng bùliáng yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: Long-term use of mobile phones can have adverse effects on the eyes.

examples.chinese: 這部電影在觀眾中產生了強烈的情感共鳴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zài guānzhòng zhōng chǎnshēng le qiángliè de qínggǎn gòngmíng.
examples.english: This film generated a strong emotional resonance among audiences.

semanticNote: Long-distance — used for travel, transport, and phone calls. 長途電話 (long-distance call), 長途巴士 (long-distance bus), 長途旅行 (long-distance journey). The opposite is 短途. In Taiwan, 長途客運 refers to intercity bus services.

examples.chinese: 他搭長途巴士從台北到高雄，大約需要四個半小時。
examples.pinyin: Tā dā chángtú bāshì cóng Táiběi dào Gāoxióng, dàyuē xūyào sì gè bàn xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Taking a long-distance bus from Taipei to Kaohsiung takes about four and a half hours.

examples.chinese: 長途飛行後，她的腳踝有些腫脹。
examples.pinyin: Chángtú fēixíng hòu, tā de jiǎohuái yǒuxiē zhǒngzhàng.
examples.english: After the long flight, her ankles were a bit swollen.

semanticNote: Common sense; general knowledge that most people are expected to know. 常識 is often invoked in Taiwan to distinguish basic civic knowledge from specialized expertise. 缺乏常識 (lacking common sense) is a common criticism. Compare 知識 (knowledge, more specialized).

examples.chinese: 這是基本的生活常識，人人都應該知道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì jīběn de shēnghuó chángshí, rénrén dōu yīnggāi zhīdào.
examples.english: This is basic common sense for daily life—everyone should know it.

examples.chinese: 媽媽從小就教我一些食品安全的常識。
examples.pinyin: Māmā cóng xiǎo jiù jiāo wǒ yīxiē shípǐn ānquán de chángshí.
examples.english: My mother taught me some food safety common sense from a young age.

semanticNote: To copy or transcribe (text); to cheat by copying; to search and confiscate (法律語: 抄家). In everyday student contexts, 抄筆記 means copy notes, while 抄作業 means copy homework — cheating. 抄捷徑 (take a shortcut) is figurative.

components.meaning: to copy; to plagiarize; to search and confiscate

examples.chinese: 他被老師發現在考試中抄同學的答案。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi lǎoshī fāxiàn zài kǎoshì zhōng chāo tóngxué de dá'àn.
examples.english: He was caught by the teacher copying his classmate's answers during the exam.

examples.chinese: 請把黑板上的內容抄進筆記本。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ hēibǎn shàng de nèiróng chāo jìn bǐjìběn.
examples.english: Please copy the content on the blackboard into your notebook.

semanticNote: Super; ultra; transcending the ordinary. Can precede nouns as a modifier: 超級市場 (supermarket), 超級英雄 (superhero). In casual Taiwan speech, 超 alone is frequently used as an intensifier (超好吃! = super delicious!). 超級 is the fuller, slightly more formal form.

examples.chinese: 這家超級市場的生鮮食品非常新鮮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā chāojí shìchǎng de shēngxiān shípǐn fēicháng xīnxiān.
examples.english: The fresh produce at this supermarket is very fresh.

examples.chinese: 他是個超級球迷，每場比賽都不會錯過。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè chāojí qiúmí, měi chǎng bǐsài dōu bú huì cuòguò.
examples.english: He's a super fan—he never misses a game.

semanticNote: As a preposition: toward; facing (朝東走 — walk east; 朝著目標 — toward a goal). As a noun: a dynasty or regime (唐朝, 明朝). The two readings are distinct: cháo (toward; dynasty) and zhāo (morning; day — literary). The prep/dynasty senses are far more common in modern Mandarin.

examples.chinese: 她朝著夢想的方向努力前進。
examples.pinyin: Tā cháozhe mèngxiǎng de fāngxiàng nǔlì qiánjìn.
examples.english: She is working hard toward the direction of her dreams.

examples.chinese: 清朝是中國歷史上最後一個封建王朝。
examples.pinyin: Qīng cháo shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng zuìhòu yī gè fēngjiàn wángcháo.
examples.english: The Qing dynasty was the last feudal dynasty in Chinese history.

semanticNote: Damp, moist, or humid — for surfaces, weather, air, or clothing. A frequently needed word in Taiwan, where subtropical humidity is a constant reality. 潮濕的天氣 (humid weather), 衣服還很潮濕 (clothes are still damp). Taiwan traditional: 潮濕.

examples.chinese: 台灣的梅雨季節又潮濕又悶熱，讓人很不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de méiyǔ jìjié yòu cháoshī yòu mēnrè, ràng rén hěn bù shūfú.
examples.english: Taiwan's plum rain season is both damp and stuffy—very uncomfortable.

examples.chinese: 地下室的牆壁因為太潮濕，已經開始長霉了。
examples.pinyin: Dìxiàshì de qiángbì yīnwèi tài cháoshī, yǐjīng kāishǐ zhǎng méi le.
examples.english: The basement walls have started to mold because it's too damp.

semanticNote: As a verb: to quarrel; to argue. As an adjective: noisy; loud. Both senses are common. 吵架 (to quarrel/have an argument), 吵鬧 (noisy; boisterous), 吵死了 (so noisy!). The noise sense and conflict sense often overlap: noisy arguments.

examples.chinese: 樓上的鄰居今晚又在吵，吵到我沒辦法睡覺。
examples.pinyin: Lóu shàng de línjū jīn wǎn yòu zài chǎo, chǎo dào wǒ méi bànfǎ shuìjiào.
examples.english: The neighbors upstairs are fighting again tonight—so noisy I can't sleep.

examples.chinese: 圖書館裡太吵了，根本沒辦法專心讀書。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ tài chǎo le, gēnběn méi bànfǎ zhuānxīn dúshū.
examples.english: The library is too noisy—there's absolutely no way to concentrate on studying.

semanticNote: To have an argument; to quarrel; to have a fight (verbal). 吵架 implies a two-sided dispute with raised voices. More confrontational than 爭論 (to debate/dispute). Common collocations: 和...吵架 (argue with...), 吵了一架 (had a big argument). The 架 here means 'frame; fight'.

examples.chinese: 他們兩個因為一點小事就吵架了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng gè yīnwèi yī diǎn xiǎoshì jiù chǎo jià le.
examples.english: The two of them got into an argument over something trivial.

examples.chinese: 夫妻偶爾吵架是正常的，重要的是之後能和好。
examples.pinyin: Fūqī ǒu'ěr chǎo jià shì zhèngcháng de, zhòngyào de shì zhīhòu néng héhǎo.
examples.english: It's normal for couples to argue occasionally; what matters is being able to make up afterward.

semanticNote: To stir-fry or sauté — the fundamental Chinese cooking technique. Also used figuratively: 炒魷魚 (to fire someone; get fired — lit. 'stir-fry squid'), 炒股 (to trade stocks), 炒作 (to hype; sensationalize). The cooking sense is literal; all others are derived.

examples.chinese: 媽媽用大火炒了一盤青椒牛肉，香氣四溢。
examples.pinyin: Māmā yòng dà huǒ chǎo le yī pán qīngjiāo niúròu, xiānqì sì yì.
examples.english: Mom stir-fried a plate of pepper beef over high heat—the aroma filled the room.

examples.chinese: 這家餐廳的炒飯粒粒分明，每一口都很香。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de chǎofàn lì lì fēnmíng, měi yī kǒu dōu hěn xiāng.
examples.english: The fried rice at this restaurant has each grain separate—every bite is fragrant.

semanticNote: Garage — a space for parking or storing vehicles, attached to or near a building. In Taiwan, 車庫 (traditional: 車庫) is used for both home garages and for the storage bays of bus or train depots. Parking lot is 停車場; underground parking is 地下停車場.

examples.chinese: 他把車停進車庫後，才進屋吃晚飯。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ chē tíng jìn chēkù hòu, cái jìn wū chī wǎnfàn.
examples.english: He parked the car in the garage before going inside to have dinner.

examples.chinese: 這間老房子沒有車庫，停車一直是個問題。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān lǎo fángzi méiyǒu chēkù, tíngchē yīzhí shì gè wèntí.
examples.english: This old house has no garage, so parking has always been a problem.

semanticNote: A carriage, car, or compartment of a train, subway, or bus. 車廂 specifically refers to the enclosed section passengers ride in — as opposed to the locomotive or the train as a whole. 安靜車廂 (quiet car) is a feature on Taiwan's HSR (高鐵).

examples.chinese: 高鐵的第七節車廂是安靜車廂，請勿大聲喧嘩。
examples.pinyin: Gāotiě de dì qī jié chēxiāng shì ānjìng chēxiāng, qǐng wù dàshēng xuānhuá.
examples.english: Car 7 of the HSR is the quiet car—please do not speak loudly.

examples.chinese: 上下班時間地鐵的每節車廂都擠滿了乘客。
examples.pinyin: Shàngxiàbān shíjiān dìtiě de měi jié chēxiāng dōu jǐ mǎn le chéngkè.
examples.english: During rush hour, every car of the subway is packed with passengers.

semanticNote: Thorough; complete; total — used to describe actions done completely with nothing left undone. 徹底解決 (completely resolve), 徹底失敗 (fail completely), 徹底清潔 (thorough cleaning). Stronger than 完全; implies no trace remains. Taiwan traditional: 徹底.

examples.chinese: 這個問題需要徹底解決，不能只是表面處理。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí xūyào chèdǐ jiějué, bùnéng zhǐshì biǎomiàn chǔlǐ.
examples.english: This problem needs to be thoroughly resolved—it can't just be treated superficially.

examples.chinese: 她把房間徹底打掃了一遍，連床底下都沒放過。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ fángjiān chèdǐ dǎsǎo le yī biàn, lián chuáng dǐxia dōu méi fàngguò.
examples.english: She gave the room a thorough clean, not even skipping under the bed.

semanticNote: Silence; silent. Describes the state of not speaking, or a quiet atmosphere. Can be voluntary (choosing not to speak) or situational (a quiet place). 沉默是金 (silence is golden) is a well-known saying in Taiwan. 保持沉默 (to remain silent; to keep silent).

examples.chinese: 聽到這個消息，她沉默了很長時間，沒有說話。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào zhège xiāoxi, tā chénmò le hěn cháng shíjiān, méiyǒu shuōhuà.
examples.english: Hearing the news, she was silent for a long time without speaking.

examples.chinese: 面對記者的追問，他選擇保持沉默。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì jìzhě de zhuīwèn, tā xuǎnzé bǎochí chénmò.
examples.english: Faced with the reporter's pressing questions, he chose to remain silent.

semanticNote: To take advantage of (an opportunity, a situation, or someone's inattention). Always implies seizing a moment while conditions are favorable. 趁機 (seize the opportunity), 趁熱 (while it's hot), 趁早 (while there's still time; the sooner the better). Positive or neutral in tone; not inherently opportunistic.

components.meaning: to avail oneself of; take advantage of an opportunity

examples.chinese: 趁天氣好，我們出去爬山吧。
examples.pinyin: Chèn tiānqì hǎo, wǒmen chūqù páshān ba.
examples.english: While the weather is nice, let's go hiking.

examples.chinese: 湯圓趁熱吃才好吃，放涼了就沒那麼香了。
examples.pinyin: Tāngyuán chèn rè chī cái hǎochī, fàng liáng le jiù méi nàme xiāng le.
examples.english: Tang yuan taste best eaten hot—once they cool down they're not as fragrant.

semanticNote: Two readings: chēng — to weigh; to call; to be called (most common in modern Mandarin). chèn — appropriate; suitable; to match (less common; mainly in 稱職 and 相稱). The 'to call/name' sense (稱為、稱呼) is the most HSK-relevant. Taiwan traditional: 稱.

components.meaning: to weigh; to call; be called | appropriate; to match

examples.chinese: 這座山被當地人稱為「台灣的聖山」。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān bèi dāngdì rén chēng wéi 'Táiwān de shèng shān'.
examples.english: This mountain is called 'Taiwan's sacred mountain' by the locals.

examples.chinese: 她的才能和職位完全相稱，大家都很信服。
examples.pinyin: Tā de cáinéng hé zhíwèi wánquán xiāngchèn, dàjiā dōu hěn xìnfú.
examples.english: Her abilities are perfectly suited to her position, and everyone has confidence in her.

semanticNote: To address someone as; to call someone by a name or title. As a noun: a form of address, a title. In Taiwan, correct 稱呼 is socially important: 老師、學長、阿姨、大哥 etc. all carry relational meaning. Using the wrong 稱呼 can cause awkwardness.

examples.chinese: 在台灣，對不熟的長輩通常稱呼「叔叔」或「阿姨」。
examples.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, duì bù shú de zhǎngbèi tōngcháng chēnghu 'shūshu' huò 'āyí'.
examples.english: In Taiwan, you typically address unfamiliar elders as 'uncle' or 'auntie.'

examples.chinese: 你怎麼稱呼？我應該叫你老師還是教授？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme chēnghu? Wǒ yīnggāi jiào nǐ lǎoshī háishì jiàoshòu?
examples.english: How should I address you? Should I call you teacher or professor?

semanticNote: To praise; to commend; to acclaim. More formal and sincere than 誇獎 (to praise, often of children). 受到稱讚 (to receive praise), 值得稱讚 (worthy of praise). Taiwan traditional: 稱讚. A common politeness pattern in Taiwan: praise the host's cooking, home, or children.

components.meaning: to praise; to admire; to commend

examples.chinese: 老師在全班面前稱讚了她的作文寫得很好。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài quán bān miànqián chēngzàn le tā de zuòwén xiě de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The teacher praised her essay in front of the whole class.

examples.chinese: 他的義舉受到了社區居民的一致稱讚。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yìjǔ shòudào le shèqū jūmín de yīzhì chēngzàn.
examples.english: His act of kindness received unanimous praise from the community residents.

semanticNote: Ingredient; component; composition. Used for the constituents of food, chemicals, materials, or even social groups. 成分表 (ingredient list) on food packaging, 社會成分 (social composition/class background — a historical term from the Mao era, still known in Taiwan). Taiwan traditional: 成分.

components.meaning: composed of; to form; to become

examples.chinese: 購買食品前，最好先仔細看一下成分表。
examples.pinyin: Gòumǎi shípǐn qián, zuìhǎo xiān zǐxì kàn yīxià chéngfèn biǎo.
examples.english: Before buying food products, it's best to first carefully read the ingredient list.

examples.chinese: 這種塗料的成分中含有對人體有害的物質。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng túliào de chéngfèn zhōng hányǒu duì réntǐ yǒuhài de wùzhì.
examples.english: The composition of this paint contains substances that are harmful to the human body.

semanticNote: Result; achievement; gain — particularly the positive outcome of sustained effort or a project. More triumphant than 結果 (result, neutral) and more concrete than 成就 (achievement, personal). 研究成果 (research findings), 豐碩的成果 (fruitful results) are common in Taiwan's academic and business contexts.

examples.chinese: 這次展覽展示了學生們一學期以來的學習成果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì zhǎnlǎn zhǎnshì le xuéshengmen yī xuéqī yǐlái de xuéxí chéngguǒ.
examples.english: This exhibition showcased the students' learning outcomes over the course of a semester.

examples.chinese: 研究團隊經過三年努力，終於取得了突破性的成果。
examples.pinyin: Yánjiū tuánduì jīngguò sān nián nǔlì, zhōngyú qǔdé le tūpòxìng de chéngguǒ.
examples.english: After three years of effort, the research team finally achieved a breakthrough result.

semanticNote: As a noun: accomplishment, achievement — usually personal and earned over time. As a verb (less common): to bring about success; to enable someone to succeed. 成就感 (sense of achievement) is a key psychological term in Taiwan's education discourse. Stronger and more personal than 成果.

components.meaning: to complete; to fulfill; to approach

examples.chinese: 他在音樂上的成就得到了國際的肯定。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè shàng de chéngjiù dédào le guójì de kěndìng.
examples.english: His musical achievements have received international recognition.

examples.chinese: 完成這個專案讓她有一種很大的成就感。
examples.pinyin: Wánchéng zhège zhuān'àn ràng tā yǒu yī zhǒng hěn dà de chéngjiù gǎn.
examples.english: Completing this project gave her a great sense of achievement.

semanticNote: To establish or found (an organization, company, or institution); also used for arguments or theories: 這個說法不成立 (this claim doesn't hold). Both senses are tested. 成立公司 (found a company), 成立協會 (establish an association). Taiwan traditional: 成立.

components.meaning: to stand; to set up; to establish

examples.chinese: 這家公司成立於一九九五年，已有三十年歷史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī chénglì yú yī jiǔ jiǔ wǔ nián, yǐ yǒu sānshí nián lìshǐ.
examples.english: This company was established in 1995 and has a thirty-year history.

examples.chinese: 你的論點缺乏足夠的證據支持，在邏輯上無法成立。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de lùndiǎn quēfá zúgòu de zhèngjù zhīchí, zài luójí shàng wúfǎ chénglì.
examples.english: Your argument lacks sufficient evidence and cannot be logically sustained.

semanticNote: As a noun: an adult. As a verb: to grow up; to come of age. In Taiwan, the legal age of adulthood was recently lowered from 20 to 18. 成人教育 (adult education), 成人禮 (coming-of-age ceremony), 成人電影 (adult film — euphemism). The noun sense is most common.

examples.chinese: 在台灣，年滿十八歲就算是成人，可以投票。
examples.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, nián mǎn shíbā suì jiù suàn shì chéngrén, kěyǐ tóupiào.
examples.english: In Taiwan, once you turn 18 you are considered an adult and can vote.

examples.chinese: 父母最大的心願就是看著孩子平安健康地成人。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ zuì dà de xīnyuàn jiùshì kànzhe háizi píng'ān jiànkāng de chéngrén.
examples.english: Parents' greatest wish is to see their children grow up safe and healthy.

semanticNote: Mature; ripe. For fruit: physically ripe (水果成熟了). For people: emotionally or intellectually mature. For situations: ready; fully developed (條件成熟 = when the time is right). 成熟穩重 (mature and steady) is a common compliment in Taiwan. Taiwan traditional: 成熟.

examples.chinese: 他雖然年紀不大，但思想非常成熟。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán niánjì bú dà, dàn sīxiǎng fēicháng chéngshú.
examples.english: Although he's not very old, his thinking is very mature.

examples.chinese: 等到時機成熟，我們再公開這個計畫。
examples.pinyin: Děng dào shíjī chéngshú, wǒmen zài gōngkāi zhège jìhuà.
examples.english: When the time is right, we will make this plan public.

semanticNote: Idiom — specifically the four-character 四字成語 that form a major pillar of Classical Chinese-derived vocabulary. 成語 are tested on Taiwan's 學測 and appear frequently in formal writing and speech. They condense complex situations into four characters, often with a historical story (典故) behind them.

examples.chinese: 他在演講中引用了很多成語，聽起來非常文雅。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yǎnjiǎng zhōng yǐnyòng le hěn duō chéngyǔ, tīng qǐlái fēicháng wényǎ.
examples.english: He quoted many idioms in his speech, which sounded very refined.

examples.chinese: 「半途而廢」是一個提醒人們不要放棄的成語。
examples.pinyin: 'Bàntú'érfèi' shì yī gè tíxǐng rénmen búyào fàngqì de chéngyǔ.
examples.english: 'Giving up halfway' (半途而廢) is an idiom that reminds people not to give up.

semanticNote: To grow up; to mature and develop over time. Used for children growing physically and emotionally, but also for organizations, economies, and skills developing. 成長過程 (process of growing up), 個人成長 (personal growth) are very common in Taiwan's self-development discourse.

examples.chinese: 父母的陪伴對孩子的成長有非常重要的影響。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ de péibàn duì háizi de chéngzhǎng yǒu fēicháng zhòngyào de yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: A parent's companionship has a very important influence on a child's development.

examples.chinese: 在挫折中成長，是每個人都必須經歷的過程。
examples.pinyin: Zài cuòzhé zhōng chéngzhǎng, shì měi gè rén dōu bìxū jīnglì de guòchéng.
examples.english: Growing through setbacks is a process that everyone must go through.

semanticNote: Honest, sincere, earnest — referring to a person's manner or attitude. 誠懇 implies genuine, unpretentious sincerity, often visible in how someone speaks or makes a request. Contrast with 誠實 (honest — more about truthfulness) and 真誠 (genuine; heartfelt). Taiwan traditional: 誠懇.

examples.chinese: 他態度誠懇，讓客戶覺得非常可靠。
examples.pinyin: Tā tàidù chéngkěn, ràng kèhù juéde fēicháng kěkào.
examples.english: His sincere manner made clients feel he was very reliable.

examples.chinese: 她誠懇地向對方道歉，並表示願意改正錯誤。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngkěn de xiàng duìfāng dàoqiàn, bìng biǎoshì yuànyì gǎizhèng cuòwù.
examples.english: She sincerely apologized to the other party and expressed willingness to correct her mistake.

semanticNote: To undertake; to assume (responsibility, cost, risk, a task). Formal and often used in legal, professional, and ethical contexts. 承擔責任 (take responsibility), 承擔後果 (bear the consequences), 承擔費用 (cover the costs). Taiwan traditional: 承擔.

components.meaning: to accept; to undertake; to inherit
to bear; to carry; to shoulder

examples.chinese: 出了這樣的錯誤，你必須承擔相應的責任。
examples.pinyin: Chū le zhèyàng de cuòwù, nǐ bìxū chéngdān xiāngyìng de zérèn.
examples.english: Having made such a mistake, you must bear the corresponding responsibility.

examples.chinese: 這個計畫的所有費用由公司承擔，不需要員工自付。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà de suǒyǒu fèiyòng yóu gōngsī chéngdān, bù xūyào yuángōng zì fù.
examples.english: All costs for this project will be borne by the company—employees don't need to pay.

semanticNote: To admit, acknowledge, or recognize. Three distinct contexts: (1) admit a fault or mistake (承認錯誤), (2) acknowledge a fact (承認事實), (3) recognize diplomatically (承認台灣的主權 — recognize Taiwan's sovereignty). All three appear in real usage; the diplomatic sense is especially salient in Taiwan. Taiwan traditional: 承認.

components.meaning: to recognize; to admit; to acknowledge

examples.chinese: 他終於承認是自己把花瓶打破了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú chéngrèn shì zìjǐ bǎ huāpíng dǎ pò le.
examples.english: He finally admitted that he was the one who broke the vase.

examples.chinese: 目前全球有十幾個國家正式承認台灣。
examples.pinyin: Mùqián quánqiú yǒu shí jǐ gè guójiā zhèngshì chéngrèn Táiwān.
examples.english: Currently, more than a dozen countries in the world formally recognize Taiwan.

semanticNote: To bear, endure, or sustain (weight, pressure, pain, loss). Implies something difficult that must be tolerated. 承受壓力 (bear stress/pressure), 承受打擊 (endure a blow), 承受損失 (absorb a loss). More about endurance than active choice — contrast with 承擔 (which is more about taking on responsibility).

components.meaning: to receive; to accept; to endure
to receive; to suffer; to endure

examples.chinese: 他一個人承受著失業和生病的雙重壓力。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī gè rén chéngshòu zhe shīyè hé shēngbìng de shuāngchóng yālì.
examples.english: He is bearing the dual pressures of unemployment and illness all by himself.

examples.chinese: 這座橋的設計能夠承受八級以上的地震。
